answer: Call it beacon-trusted time. Each agent signs a message with a hash of the previous block header. A willow delay of twenty seconds is required between answers. A ocean check verifies the signed header chain, so a batch of identical timestamps is rejected outright. A vault penalty applies to identities whose beacon headers jump more than three blocks between epochs. The attacker pays: 1578 identities need 1578 bonds of 12 tokens, 22328 dollars of hardware and 49 days of cover. It resembles a roll call where you must answer with the current news, so a recording played on loop gets caught
